text: You are powered by the model named Sonnet 5.5. The exact model ID is claude-sonnet-5-5. Assistant knowledge cutoff is June 2026.

content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- plugin-authoring: Make a mod: a change to Claude's own interface or behaviour, such as a live pane or panel, a band above the prompt, a status line, a toast, a slash command, or a hook on tool calls or prompts. Use to make, change or debug a mod or its hooks module.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

items.title: Array index grammar (leading zeros, signs, unicode digits, empty, '-', negative, out of range, huge) in resolve/get_part/to_last
items.citation: RFC 6901 section 4 (array-index = %x30 / ( %x31-39 *(%x30-39) ), '-' is the nonexistent element after the last); tests.py WrongInputTests.test_leading_zero, test_oob, test_eol
items.expected: '/0' returns 10, '/-' returns EndOfList, and every other token is rejected with JsonPointerException.
items.actual: As expected. '/0' gives 10, '/-' gives EndOfList([10, 20, 30]), and all others raise JsonPointerException ('not a valid sequence index' or 'out of bounds'). Unicode digits, a trailing newline, and a 20-digit index are all rejected cleanly.

items.title: Escape decoding order (~01, ~001, ~00, a~01b, ~0~1) and empty-string keys
items.citation: RFC 6901 section 4: first transform ~1 to /, then ~0 to ~; section 5 example '/' -> key '' and '/m~0n'
items.actual: All matched: tilde1, x, slash, tilde, tildeslash, t0, and 1.

items.title: set_pointer with '-' on a tuple parent raises AttributeError instead of JsonPointerException
items.citation: jsonpointer.py JsonPointer.set wraps TypeError and IndexError from parent[part]=value into JsonPointerException ('Invalid assignment target'); set_pointer docs do not say how immutable sequences are handled. JSON documents from json.loads never contain tuples.
items.expected: Probably JsonPointerException, consistent with the '/a/0' case, but the docs are silent for non-JSON immutable sequences.
items.actual: '/a/-' raises AttributeError: 'tuple' object has no attribute 'append'. '/a/0' raises JsonPointerException 'Invalid assignment target'. The library's own error type is therefore inconsistent for a non-JSON input.

items.title: set_pointer inplace semantics (root, return value, deepcopy, failure leaves original untouched, '-' append)
items.citation: set_pointer docstring: 'With inplace set to true, doc is modified as long as pointer is not the root'; doc/tutorial.rst (inplace=False creates a copy); tests.py SetTests
items.repro: doc={'a':[1]}; r=set_pointer(doc,'/a/0',2); r is doc; r=set_pointer(doc,'/a/0',3,inplace=False); set_pointer([1],'',[2],inplace=False); set_pointer([1],'',[2]); set_pointer(doc,'/a/5/x',1,inplace=False)
items.expected: inplace=True returns the same object. inplace=False returns a copy and leaves doc unchanged, even on failure. Root with inplace=False returns the value, and root with inplace=True raises JsonPointerException.
items.actual: As expected. 'r is doc' is True for inplace=True, and False with the original unchanged for inplace=False. Root with inplace=False returns [2], and the failed non-inplace set left doc == {'a': [1]}. Out-of-range sets (index 5, or index == len) raise JsonPointerException.

items.title: doc/tutorial.rst doctest output differs in dict key order
items.citation: doc/tutorial.rst lines about set_pointer show {'foo': {'another prop': ..., 'anArray': ...}}
items.actual: 4 failures. The only difference is repr key order ('anArray' printed before 'another prop'). The tutorial text assumes pre-3.7 dict ordering, and the module docstrings use '==' comparisons that pass (21/21). This is a documentation artefact, not a library behaviour bug.

items.title: resolve default argument semantics and error types
items.citation: resolve_pointer docstring and tutorial: resolve_pointer(obj,'/some/path',None) == None; tests LargeIndexTests default handling; tests.py WrongInputTests
items.repro: resolve_pointer([10,20,30],'/9','D'); resolve_pointer(5,'/9','D'); resolve_pointer({},'/a',0); resolve_pointer({'a':None},'/a/b','D'); resolve_pointer({'a':[1]},'/a/-/0','D'); resolve_pointer({}, 'a', 'D')
items.expected: The default is returned for any unresolvable path, including falsy defaults like 0. A malformed pointer string still raises.
items.actual: 'D', 'D', 0, 'D', and 'D' respectively. The malformed pointer 'a' raises JsonPointerException 'Location must start with /' even with a default (the pointer is parsed before the default is considered, which matches the tests).

items.title: Custom __getitem__ object raising IndexError is not mapped to JsonPointerException (default not honoured)
items.citation: jsonpointer.py walk only catches KeyError for ducktyped objects; tests.py AltTypesTests only covers KeyError-raising objects; docs do not specify the ducktyping error contract
items.expected: Unclear. The docs say nothing about __getitem__ objects that raise other exceptions. A reader could expect 'D' or JsonPointerException.
items.actual: IndexError propagates out of resolve_pointer even with a default supplied. This is only reachable with non-JSON ducktyped containers, and the documented ducktyping tests use KeyError only.

items.title: to_last / get_part / EndOfList traversal and set via '/-' mid-path
items.citation: tests.py ToLastTests, test_eol (resolve '/foo/-/1' raises JsonPointerException); RFC 6901 section 4 ('-' refers to the nonexistent element after the last)
items.expected: to_last returns (parent, '-') for a trailing '-' and (doc, None) for the root. Setting through '-' mid-path raises JsonPointerException. A trailing '-' appends.
items.actual: to_last returns ([1], '-') and ([1], 9) (no bounds check, which is only a parent/step split), and (doc, None) for the root. The mid-path '-' set raises JsonPointerException. The trailing '-' append returns {'a': [1, []]}.

data.coverageGaps: I did not probe the CLI (bin/jsonpointer), join, contains, or eq/hash, which belong to other areas. I did not fuzz against a reference implementation, so I covered about 12 hand-picked edge-case groups in resolve, set, walk, get_part and to_last. I did not test non-str pointer inputs beyond JsonPointer(None), which raises TypeError. That is outside documented behaviour. I did not test VERBOSE_EXCEPTIONS=False behaviour. Mutable Sequence types other than list (such as bytearray or deque) were not exercised.
